area_summary: Almost all text and special-screen 2D in this area goes through one choke point: draw functions call dComIfGp_getCurrentGrafPort()->setPort() and J2DScreen::draw(0,0,graf). That grafport is the J2DOrthoGraph built in mDoGph_Painter (m_Do_graphic.cpp:1572-1574 and again at 1890-1891; ortho box -9,-21..650,503 from the shared constants @5162/@5163 at 0x803F7D68/0x803F7D6C, loaded at mDoGph_Painter+0x110/+0x120/+0xAD4/+0xAE4). The 2D particles (m_Do_graphic.cpp:1894-1922; JPA uses the aspect only for projected-texture matrices) and the 2D drawlist primitives (dDlst_2Dm_c and the rest) draw with the same projection. J2D pane clipping turns ortho units into pixels through J2DOrthoGraph::scissorBounds (0x802CDD84), so it follows an ortho-based compression too. So the global compression, done by widening that ortho about its centre, already fixes the text boxes, item-get box, choice arrows, button icons, song notes, metronome, minigame start/finish text, timers and the message part of the picto box. No per-screen work is needed there; the text boxes are bottom-centre or centre anchored. **Cheap but needed:** two shared helpers in T2, (1) ws_project2d(src,dst), which calls mDoLib_project and then maps x back out of the compression (x' = c + (x - c)*F, c = the compression centre, 320.5 for the vanilla -9..650 box), and (2) ws_screen_draw_full(J2DScreen*, x, y, graf), which puts back the vanilla ortho, calls J2DScreen::draw (0x802D0F2C), then restores the compressed one, plus a side-fill call (J2DFillBox 0x802CDF3C). Each is used by replacing one `bl` with hook_branchlink. **Expensive or design decisions:** (a) the picto box: the photo capture, the snap judge and the photo display all work in raw EFB pixels with private orthos. The cleanest model keeps the whole picto pipeline uncompressed (the frame drawn full width, photos anamorphic) and scales the pixel-count thresholds by F; that is about 7 hook sites but no data changes. (b) THP movies (the title loop and the whole staff roll, end_st_epilogue.thp, both 640x480) live in a loose, Yaz0-compressed REL that is loaded before our REL exists, so pillarboxing needs a T2 per-frame write into the REL's .bss. (c) Full-screen masks that are J2D panes (telescope black, game-over black, Wind's Requiem dimmer, the opening legend) need full-width treatment per screen. That is one bl hook each, as Dolphin's Gecko code does with `li r4,0` (a NULL grafport, which falls back to a fresh 0..640 ortho; J2DScreen.cpp:154-158). (d) Minigame HUD primitives with hard-coded edge positions (the cannon game, Sploosh Kaboom, the timer's rupee/icon at x=32) need left or right edge anchoring. Placement: the title, opening and movie fixes must be in T2, because the REL only loads after Link exists plus 300 frames. The in-game ones (text box, picto, scope, timers) could sit behind T2 trampolines into the REL if T2 space runs short. None of the sites below is already hooked in build.py; the nearest is seachart_shim at 0x801BB06C. Gecko's code caves (0x800037E0, 0x80004038) sit in CanaryTRK and must not be reused.

open_questions: Every item assumes the shared fix compresses 2D by widening the grafport ortho box in mDoGph_Painter (m_Do_graphic.cpp:1573 and 1890, constants 0x803F7D68/0x803F7D6C, which setUpRectangle 0x8000A530 also reads). If the shared fix uses the viewport or a different centre instead, the ws_project2d centre c, the Δleft/Δright values and ws_screen_draw_full's restore have to match it. Rewriting those two .sdata2 constants also compresses the picto preview (setUpRectangle), which conflicts with Option A. Prefer patching the Painter's lfs sites or setOrtho calls over the constants.

Picto box product decision: Option A (frame full width, wider anamorphic photos, thresholds scaled by F) or Option B (true 4:3 photos, a software resample in mCaptureProc, plus a narrower judge rect and a compressed frame and display). Option A is far cheaper and keeps the window and photo consistent.

THP pillarbox: confirm live that the .bss offsets from the disc map (xSize at bss+0xCB580, DrawPosX at bss+0xCB59C) and the bss address from the OS module list are right, and that the side bands are cleared black on the title and in the ending.

Who sets mode 2 before the title screen? ws_init's C default is mode 1 (culling plan 6.1). Native mode at the title (THP, opening legend) needs either a C default of 2 or a persistent setting the C side can read at boot.

Pane layouts not visible in the decomp (wipe_01_01.blo, Opening.blo, auction blo, Sploosh set_2dposition in a stub-only REL): screenshot each in mode 2, or parse the blo from the disc, to confirm which panes are full-screen masks and which elements sit at the edges.

The game-over, Wind's Requiem and opening masks: decide whether to use the cheap full-screen redraw (stretched letters or art, as Gecko does) or to widen only the backdrop pane. A widened pane needs the pane pointer (e.g. dDlst_GameOverScrnDraw_c::blak) and restoring when the mode changes.

T2 budget: about 12 hook_branchlink sites plus 4 helpers (roughly 0x300-0x450 bytes) on top of the culling hook. The in-game ones (picto, scope, text box, timer, minigame vtables) could forward into the REL when T2 is short; the title, legend and movie ones cannot, because they run before the REL loads.
